name: NullPoint Technologies CortexVeil CV-1 'Deadzone'
description:
A self-defense headband that creates a personal electromagnetic cocoon around the wearer's own neural interface, protecting against external BCI intrusion attempts. Unlike NullPoint's offensive products that disrupt attackers' augmentations, the CV-1 is purely defensive — it generates a precisely calibrated interference pattern that blocks unauthorized wireless access to the wearer's BCI without disrupting the interface's normal function.

The CV-1 addresses a growing threat in GLMZ: neural hacking. As BCI technology has become ubiquitous, so have tools for wireless BCI intrusion — devices that can access a victim's neural interface to inject sensory hallucinations, read surface thoughts, trigger pain responses, or disable motor control. These attacks are difficult to detect and nearly impossible to defend against without hardware-level protection. The CV-1 provides that protection in a wearable form factor.

The headband uses a thin conductive mesh that, when powered, generates a white-noise electromagnetic shell around the wearer's cranial BCI hardware. This shell is transparent to the wearer's own BCI signals (which are calibrated during a one-time setup process) but blocks external signals that don't match the authorized pattern. The CV-1 costs Φ450 and is available in several widths and fabric covers to blend with different styles. NullPoint's marketing for the CV-1 is notably more mainstream than their offensive products — protecting your own brain is a less controversial proposition than disrupting someone else's.
specifications:
protection type: blocks unauthorized wireless BCI access
effect on wearer's BCI: none (calibrated during setup)
setup: one-time 10-minute calibration per BCI model
battery life: 18 hours continuous
charging: wireless induction, 1 hour
weight: 45 g
form factor: headband, multiple width/color options
cost: Φ450
compatible BCI models: all consumer and most commercial-grade interfaces
tactical_use: Wear continuously when in public spaces. The CV-1 provides passive protection against wireless BCI intrusion without requiring activation or attention. The one-time calibration process ensures the headband does not interfere with normal BCI function. If you suspect an active intrusion attempt, the CV-1's indicator LED (hidden on the inner surface) will pulse red. In environments where neural hacking is common, wearing the CV-1 is not optional — it is baseline security hygiene.
cultural_context: The CV-1 has become the BCI equivalent of a condom — protection so obvious that not using it is considered reckless. The street nickname 'Neural Condom' captures both the protective function and the cultural normalcy of the device. In augmented communities, wearing a CV-1 or equivalent is expected, and not wearing one is seen as either naive or inviting trouble. NullPoint's success with the CV-1 has spawned an entire category of 'neural hygiene' products, but the CV-1 remains the market leader.
story_hooks: A flaw in the CV-1's calibration process has been discovered — if exploited during setup, an attacker can register their own signal pattern as 'authorized,' gaining permanent undetected access to the wearer's BCI through the very device meant to protect it.

A Tier 1 community health program is distributing free CV-1 units to augmented residents — but the units were donated by an anonymous corporate sponsor, raising questions about whether the headbands contain a backdoor.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, minimalist headband with a subtle futuristic aesthetic—more medical device than fashion accessory, though designed to blend into everyday wear. The form factor suggests both utility and discretion, sitting low across the forehead and temples without drawing attention.
physical_description.dimensions: Circumference adjusts 54–62 cm. Width across forehead: 3.2 cm. Depth at temples: 1.8 cm. Total height when worn: approximately 2.5 cm above scalp.
physical_description.weight_description: Exceptionally light and balanced—barely noticeable once worn. The 45g weight is distributed evenly to prevent fatigue during extended wear.
physical_description.primary_material: Conductive mesh composite woven with flexible polymer skeleton. The mesh itself is a silver-threaded nano-weave embedded in a soft elastomer backing.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal with subtle metallic shimmer where the conductive mesh is visible. The mesh itself has a brushed-silver appearance with faint blue undertones from embedded circuit pathways.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary with silver-blue conductive threading visible beneath translucent sections. Accent colors vary by model—matte black, midnight blue, or gunmetal options available.
physical_description.grip_texture: The inner surface (against skin) is soft, moisture-wicking elastomer with a faint grip pattern. The outer band has a smooth, slightly rubberized texture for stability. Adjustable fabric covers available in cotton-poly blend or synthetic leather.
distinctive_features: Hidden status LED (inner temple surface, only visible to wearer) pulses red during intrusion attempts
Barely visible silver-thread conductive mesh pattern throughout the band—more apparent under direct light
Wireless induction charging contacts recessed along the rear temples (rose-gold plating)
Adjustment micro-clasps at both temples with tactile click-feedback
Faint etched serial number and model designation on the rear band (CV-1)
Temperature-responsive fabric sections that lighten/darken slightly with body heat
Ultra-thin profile allows seamless wear under hats, hoods, or hair
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: NullPoint Technologies logo (stylized Φ symbol with neural nodes) embossed on rear center clasp. Small 'CV-1 DEADZONE' text laser-etched into left temple clasp. FCC/GLMZ compliance stamp on interior back band.
physical_description.condition_typical: Maintained in pristine to lightly worn condition. Regular users show minimal wear—occasional creasing where adjustment clasps operate, faint discoloration on inner elastomer from perspiration (normal and inconsequential). Some units show light dust accumulation on the silver mesh, giving them a slightly aged aesthetic after months of continuous use.
